dossiers.thesis_summary: Green Dot is being acquired via a definitive agreement (signed 23 Nov 2025): CommerceOne takes Green Dot Bank into a NEW publicly-traded bank holding company and Smith Ventures privatizes the fintech ops; GDOT holders receive $8.11 cash + 0.2215 shares of the unlisted NewCo per share (fixed ratio, no collar). Both shareholder votes cleared 23 June 2026. Remaining condition is bank-regulatory approval (Fed Section 3, Alabama State Banking Dept, Utah DFI) plus HSR — none announced as of 20 Jul 2026; Section 3 application only Fed-Register-noticed 6 Apr 2026. Company guides a Q3-2026 close (already slipped once from Q2-2026); contractual outside date 23 Nov 2026, extendable to 23 Feb 2027. This is an impure merger arb: ~40% of consideration is an unlisted, unhedgeable bank-holdco stub, so the residual is a directional bet on NewCo's day-one listing multiple, not a lockable spread.
dossiers.kill_risk: The break floor is a point estimate on a wide, unhedgeable distribution: on a Fed refusal GDOT is not worthless (valuable bank charter + fintech relationship, Citi could re-run a process), so the standalone floor could hold above ~$10 rather than my ~$9.75 — but a supervisory rejection mid-dismemberment argues the other way. Symmetric residual: if the deal closes (~80%+) AND the NewCo stub lists at/above 1.0x TBV, the company's $14.23-$19.18 illustration is realizable, so a stub-holder could earn real upside from spot — meaning my "edge is spent, fair value ≈ spot" claim only holds for someone who cannot/will not carry the unlisted stub through listing.

dossiers.thesis_summary: UNF is a live single-stock merger-arb spread: Cintas (CTAS) acquires UniFirst under a definitive agreement (signed 10 Mar 2026) for FIXED consideration of $155.00 cash + 0.7720 CTAS shares, NO collar. Shareholder approval satisfied 12 Jun 2026. The only open condition is US antitrust: FTC issued a Second Request 11 Jun 2026, extending HSR until 30 days after substantial compliance — an UNDATED event (no calendar date), company-guided to close 2H calendar 2026. Idiosyncratic (resolves on FTC's competitive analysis of uniform-rental concentration, not the tape). At live prices (UNF $289.99, CTAS $201.09) deal value = $155 + 0.7720×201.09 = $310.24, so capped upside is only +$20.25 (+7.0%); the break floor sits at UNF's unaffected standalone (~$168, the Dec-2025 90-day avg implied by Cintas' own re-bid release), i.e. ~-42% downside. Break-even close probability ~86%. Terms fixed, upside capped, and the cap floats with CTAS.
dossiers.kill_risk: My load-bearing claim is that the break floor is ~$168 (unaffected standalone), making downside ~-42% vs +7% capped upside. Residual risk: (a) the floor may be higher than $168 — UNF reported FY26-Q3 on 1 Jul 2026 with an active margin-improvement program, so post-Q3 standalone value could have re-rated above the Dec-2025 unaffected anchor, and a break could draw a rival strategic/PE bid given the sector's scarcity value; (b) the break-fee (~$19.36/sh) is payable only in specified regulatory-breach circumstances, so it partly cushions some (not all) break paths, lifting the effective floor toward ~$187 in those cases; (c) the cap itself floats up with CTAS, so a further CTAS rally widens the win value above $310. None of these overturns the core fact set: undated antitrust event, contractually capped upside, floor well below spot.

dossiers.thesis_summary: FTAI Infrastructure (FIP) is the SELLER of Long Ridge Energy & Power to a MARA Holdings subsidiary for ~$1.52B (definitive agreement Apr 29-30, 2026). The resolving event is FERC Section 203 authorization in docket EC26-92-000 (joint application filed May 8, 2026; comments closed May 29, 2026 with a PJM IMM request to condition; no Commission order as of July 17, 2026). Management guided approval to mid-Q3 2026 with FERC the only material condition (HSR/STB customary; no buyer financing condition; $75M reverse break fee; buyer bondholder change-of-control consents already secured May 14-15, 2026; outside date Nov 30, 2026, extendable up to 7 months). Catalyst is real, forward-dated, unfired, and idiosyncratic (resolves on FERC ruling, not the tape). CRITICAL VALUATION FACT: because FIP is the seller, closing delivers ~$1.16B Long Ridge debt elimination, ~$300M parent-level debt repayment and ~$30M/yr interest relief — deleveraging, NOT a per-share consideration to common. The board's $9 target is an undated analyst sum-of-the-parts on the RESIDUAL company (Transtar rail, Jefferson, Repauno), which sits behind ~$1.59B of redemption-value preferred (Series A RailCo ~$1.4B + Series B ~$192M) on negative common equity — it is a second, unforced, undated re-rate, not event-resolved value.
dossiers.kill_risk: Even a clean FERC approval and close does NOT deliver the $9: closing pays down parent debt (~$300M) and saves ~$30M/yr interest, but the residual common is a levered stub standing behind ~$1.59B of redemption-value preferred (Series A RailCo redeemable at ~$1,417.49/sh = ~$1.4B, mandatorily redeemable on a rail-business sale, accreting ~$108-129M/yr in kind — outrunning the $30M/yr saved) on total equity of NEGATIVE ~$303M (Q1 2026 10-Q, period 3/31/26), $37.9M unrestricted cash, $3.84B total debt. The $9 SoP requires a second undated re-rate the catalyst itself does not force. Worse, the same 10-Q states the going-concern liquidity plan is alleviated BY the Long Ridge sale — so a deal break does not produce a bounded loss, it removes the stated liquidity plan; downside is undefined, not floored at $3.90 (floor and catalyst are the same object → negatively correlated). The event verifies; the valuation axes the board used do not.

dossiers.thesis_summary: FIG (Figma) is a lockup-unlock / forced-seller situation, not a sum-of-parts. The final Extended Lock-Up tranche — the ~77.7M-share Class A remainder held by ~54.1%-of-Class-A holders — releases at the open on Fri 2026-08-07, triggered by Q2 earnings after close Wed 2026-08-05 (contractual: earlier of the 2nd trading day post-earnings or 2026-08-31). This is a real, dated, unfired, idiosyncratic event, but it adds supply against a long; the favorable resolution the seat needs (overhang absorbed, multiple re-rates) is undated and soft — venture distribution runs for weeks/quarters after release. Financially this is a single high-multiple SaaS equity (~7.6x EV/2026 rev), not a recovery/SoP claim: Q1 FY26 rev $333.4M (+46%, guiding 40% Q2 / 35% FY), GAAP op loss $137.4M, SBC $169M (50.7% of rev). The only structural floor is net cash: $1.638B cash+securities, no debt, /528.4M sh = ~$3.10/sh — the board's $17.5 floor and $32 target are revenue-multiple assumptions, not structural anchors.

dossiers.thesis_summary: BLCO is held on a "forced divest flow" special-situation: parent Bausch Health (BHC, ~87% / 310,449,643 shares) is expected to monetize or spin its Bausch + Lomb stake, surfacing a sum-of-parts / takeout value (~$27 board target). Deep re-underwrite from the live record REFUTES the forced-seller mechanism. The separation is real only as a soft, undated, parent-controlled intent ("may include monetization... transfer... or a combination"), serially extended ~6 years, and is contractually blocked: ~68% of BHC's stake (211,963,893 shares held by 126NumberCo) is pledged under a first-priority lien securing the 2030 Term Loan B + 2032 Senior Secured Notes, with a 100% net-cash-proceeds sweep to secured creditors on any sale of the collateral and a distribution bar while the lien attaches. So a monetization pays lenders, not BHC equity, and a spin cannot transfer pledged shares — out to 2030-2032. There is no forcing function: Apr-2025 and Dec-2025 refinancings pushed ~$8.5B of maturities from 2025-2028 into 2030-2032, and the separation is gated on a parent-controlled "targeted debt leverage" threshold. The one "live wire" the board scored (a supposed Federal Circuit rifaximin patch appeal) was misattributed and already fired FAVORABLY for Bausch on 26 June 2026 (D.C. Circuit, Norwich v. Kennedy — FDA correctly withheld final generic-Xifaxan approval to Oct 2029), producing no separation date.
dossiers.kill_risk: The forced-divest thesis is dead as a dated catalyst, but the separation intent and B+L's standalone quality are real, so revival optionality is non-zero: (a) only ~68% of BHC's stake is pledged/swept — BHC could sell the unpledged ~19-32% or use improving leverage to refinance/release the collateral earlier than 2030; (b) a strategic buyer could still bid for the whole company at a premium that clears the sweep and re-rates BLCO (Blackstone/TPG looked at ~$25 in 2024-25). Countervailing: near-term gradual open-market equity sales by BHC are a supply OVERHANG that pressures BLCO, not a value-surfacing event. Net: real but undated, un-forced, and out-of-the-money on the proceeds sweep — not a Basket-13-grade live catalyst.

dossiers.dossier_note:
STATUS: BROKEN, catalyst_live=false. Two independent structural kills, both consistent with BHC's Q1-2026 10-Q (period ended 31 Mar 2026) and the parent's public framing.

(1) PROCEEDS SWEEP / LIEN BLOCK. 126NumberCo owns 211,963,893 B+L shares (~59.5% of BLCO shares out, ~68% of BHC's 310,449,643 stake) pledged under a first-priority lien securing the 2030 Revolver + 2030 Term Loan B and, pari passu, the 10.00% 2032 Senior Secured Notes. The 2030 TLB carries a 100% net-cash-proceeds sweep on any sale/disposition of the B+L Share Collateral, and the 2032 Notes are subject to mandatory redemption on those proceeds. Consequence: a monetization pays BHC's secured creditors, not BHC equity — which is precisely why BHC could walk from reported ~$25/sh (Blackstone/TPG, Feb-2025) and feel nothing. A distribution route is also blocked: pledged collateral cannot be transferred to shareholders while the lien attaches. Gated to 2030-2032, third-party lenders hold the veto.

(2) NO FORCING FUNCTION + TRIGGER SPENT. Apr-2025 refi extended ~$6,870M and Dec-2025 exchange a further ~$1,600M of maturities into 2030-2032 — the parent is under LESS clock pressure than at underwriting. The separation remains "subject to the achievement of targeted debt leverage ratios," a threshold BHC never quantified and wholly controls. The board's scored "live wire" (11 Dec 2025 argument, framed as a Federal Circuit patent appeal that could accelerate generic Xifaxan) was misattributed: it was the D.C. Circuit APA case Norwich v. Kennedy, decided 26 Jun 2026 FOR Bausch (FDA correctly enjoined final Norwich ANDA approval to Oct 2029). It fired favorably ~3 weeks before verification and produced no Form 10, no registration statement, no separation date.

VALUATION AXES (method=sop, but the SoP-unlock premise is refuted, so the $27 target is a conditional cap, not fair value):
- Board target $26.97 is unreproducible. Real-world price discovery: the 2024-25 sale process topped ~$25 and failed; and on the sweep, marginal sale dollars accrue to lenders. Standalone fair-value anchor = 13-analyst consensus $18.13 (Buy), ~13% above spot $16.07.
- Downside floor corrected $11.80 -> $11.00: already broke (close $11.00, 8 Apr 2025) against ~4.6x leverage, trailing net loss, negative Q1 FCF, and no deal to break.
- Board R:R 3.49 does not survive: on a defensible ($18.13 up / $11.00 down) frame from $16.07, upside ~$2.06 vs downside ~$5.07 = ~0.4:1 — inverted. resolution_driver corrected to Refi_restructuring: the only thing that unlocks the separation is parent deleveraging/refi releasing the secured-debt block, not a forced flow. CFO (Q1-2026 call) confirms the route is gradual open-market equity sales — a supply overhang, not a value-surfacing catalyst.

dossiers.thesis_summary: The resolving event has FIRED. dossiers.thesis_summary: Binary Phase 3 LUCIDITY topline readout (avexitide in post-bariatric hypoglycemia), guided Q3 2026 and unfired. Avexitide is a first-in-class GLP-1 receptor antagonist with FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation testing an FDA-agreed composite (Level 2+3 hypoglycemic event) endpoint in a 16-wk, n=78, randomized double-blind trial; enrollment completed 24-Mar-2026. Success (~$28) vs failure (~$4) resolves overnight on ~78 participants.
dossiers.kill_risk: The pivotal 90mg QD dose has NEVER been tested blinded vs placebo on the LUCIDITY composite endpoint. The supporting 64% composite reduction came from open-label investigator-initiated crossover NCT04652479 (n=16, no placebo, no blinding); the only blinded placebo-controlled data (PREVENT, n=18) measured a different primary endpoint (post-meal glucose nadir) at different doses. So a PoS above the market-implied ~58% is not defensible — open-label, symptom-logged event counts are exactly where effect sizes decay under blinding, and win_prob 0.60 is barely above market (no real edge). Secondary: the $4 downside floor is soft, not hard — it credits ~$1.5-2/sh above net cash, and this same team's PHOENIX ALS failure (Mar-2024) drove the stock THROUGH net cash on continued-burn fears, so a miss could break toward ~$2.50/sh gross cash.

dossiers.thesis_summary: SoP / discount-to-NAV unlock: LBTYK (~$10) trades far below an ~$18 sum-of-parts as Liberty Global consolidates its Benelux assets (VodafoneZiggo + Telenet) into Ziggo Group and plans a 2H-2027 Euronext Amsterdam spin of the 90% stake to holders, intended to narrow the holdco discount.
dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim -- a spin that crystallizes the NAV discount -- is undated and unobligated: Liberty Global's own 8-K conditions the spin on board approval, an SEC-effective registration statement (none filed), and shareholder approval, and its releases say only that it "plans to" spin in 2H-2027 (a 6-month window, ~12-18 months out). The definitive agreement obligates the Vodafone BUY, not the SPIN. The $9.50 "floor" is not backstopped (no break fee, CVR, or cash-out -- it is a JV buy-in, not a takeout of LBTYK), so downside is open below spot, which is already at a fresh 26-week low. ~65% of the $3.4B Liberty Growth FMV is five illiquid private marks (a model output, not a tested asset), and the spin newly consolidates VodafoneZiggo's ~EUR 10.4B net debt. Per the skeptic, the index-flow mechanic is also inverted -- forced selling lands on the Ziggo Group line post-distribution, not on LBTYK pre-distribution (Sunrise 2024 precedent: parent stub did not re-rate).
